newsitem.title: USA: Benetton plans new campaign to break into U.S. market.
newsitem.headline: Benetton plans new campaign to break into U.S. market.

text.p: Italian clothing company Benetton Group is opening another campaign to break into the huge U.S. market, this time with million-dollar superstores, Chairman Luciano Benetton said Tuesday.

Benetton told Reuters that Wednesday's official opening of the new flagship store on New York's posh Fifth Avenue marks a switch to bigger stores that will carry all the company's brands, including sporting goods.

The company, known for controversial advertising campaigns that included pictures of AIDS victims and mourners at a corpse's bedside, plans to open megastores in 10 U.S. cities and in Europe by autumn 1997.
"This shop on Fifth Avenue is going to be the starting point for this type of evolution toward shops of larger dimensions," Benetton said through an interpreter.

The move is part of Benetton's effort to maintain itself in the $110 billion U.S. apparel market, he said, adding, "We wanted ... to feel at home in the United States, although it is true that there have been better periods in the past."

The number of Benetton stores has fallen to about 200 from a peak in 1988 of about 600 under harsh U.S. competition. Benetton's U.S. sales are about $150 million a year, or about 5 percent of worldwide sales.
Asked what percentage the company had of the U.S. market, Benetton said, "We don't really like to think about that because otherwise we would feel very small."

The 13,000-square-foot (2,070-square-metre) flagship store is in the former Charles Scribner's Sons building, a 1913 Beaux Arts structure designated a New York City landmark and restored by Benetton for $4 million. A similar store opened in London in September.

Benetton, a co-founder of the company, said the new stores probably would cost between $1 million and $2 million each to build. Cities hosting them will include Miami, Chicago, San Francisco, Los Angeles and Boston.
The megastores for the first time will carry clothing lines along with athletic equipment from such Benetton companies as Nordica ski boots, Rollerblade in-line skates and Ektelon racquet gear.

Carlo Gilardi, the chief executive of Benetton Group, who also attended the interview with other officials, said the company expected to see a 9 percent increase in revenues for the second half of 1996 compared with the same period last year.
Benetton Group saw a similar increase in the first half of 1996. Revenues last year totalled 2.94 trillion lire, or about $2 billion.

Gianni Mion, the chief executive of Benetton Sportsystem SpA, the sports equipment unit, said Benetton was weighing splitting off the division as a publicly traded company. However, he said, there was no timetable for such a move.
